title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Diabetes Self-Management Education by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with Type 2 diabetes in Medicaid populations, particularly Hispanic/Latino and African American communities
implementation_guidance: Implement 6-session culturally tailored diabetes education program using CFIR framework. Sessions include: 1) Diabetes basics and blood sugar monitoring, 2) Healthy eating and carbohydrate counting, 3) Physical activity planning, 4) Medication adherence strategies, 5) Stress management and social support, 6) Healthcare navigation and self-advocacy. Each session 90 minutes, delivered in community settings.
expected_outcomes: Significant reduction in HbA1c levels (mean decrease 0.8-1.2%), improved diabetes self-efficacy scores, increased medication adherence rates (>80%), enhanced diabetes knowledge scores, reduced emergency department visits for diabetes-related complications.
evidence_base: Kim K, Choi JS, Choi E, Nieman CL, Joo JH, Lin FR, Gitlin LN, Han HR. Effects of Community-Based Health Worker Interventions to Improve Chronic Disease Management and Care Among Vulnerable Populations: A Systematic Review. Am J Public Health. 2016;106(4):e3-e28.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Hypertension Medication Adherence by Care Coordinators
target_population: Adults with hypertension in Medicaid populations with medication adherence challenges
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic medication adherence intervention using motivational interviewing and behavioral strategies. Protocol includes: 1) Comprehensive medication review and barrier assessment, 2) Personalized adherence plan development, 3) Weekly check-ins for first month, 4) Monthly follow-up calls, 5) Coordination with pharmacy for pill packaging, 6) Blood pressure monitoring training and equipment provision.
expected_outcomes: Improved medication adherence rates (>85%), significant reduction in systolic blood pressure (mean decrease 12-15 mmHg), reduced cardiovascular events, improved patient satisfaction with care coordination, decreased healthcare utilization for hypertension-related complications.
evidence_base: Carter BL, Rogers M, Daly J, Zheng S, James PA. The potency of team-based care interventions for hypertension: a meta-analysis. Arch Intern Med. 2009;169(19):1748-1755.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Depression Screening and Referral by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults in primary care settings, particularly those with chronic conditions and social determinants of health challenges
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic depression screening using PHQ-9 with warm handoff protocol. Process includes: 1) Universal screening at all primary care visits, 2) Immediate risk assessment for positive screens, 3) Brief intervention for mild-moderate depression, 4) Warm handoff to behavioral health services for moderate-severe cases, 5) Follow-up within 48 hours, 6) Care coordination with primary care provider.
expected_outcomes: Increased depression screening rates (>90%), improved detection of depression cases, reduced time to treatment initiation, improved depression outcomes (PHQ-9 score reduction >50%), enhanced patient satisfaction with integrated care, reduced no-show rates for behavioral health appointments.
evidence_base: O'Connor EA, Whitlock EP, Beil TL, Gaynes BN. Screening for depression in adult patients in primary care settings: a systematic evidence review. Ann Intern Med. 2009;151(11):793-803.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Social Determinants Screening and Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Vulnerable populations in healthcare settings with housing, food, transportation, and financial insecurity
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive social determinants screening and resource connection protocol. Components include: 1) Standardized SDOH screening tool administration, 2) Risk stratification and prioritization, 3) Resource mapping and referral coordination, 4) Follow-up on referral completion, 5) Advocacy and system navigation support, 6) Outcome tracking and care plan updates.
expected_outcomes: Improved access to social services (>75% successful referral completion), reduced food insecurity rates, improved housing stability, enhanced healthcare access and utilization, reduced emergency department visits for non-medical needs, improved patient-reported quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Gottlieb L, Tobey R, Cantor J, Hessler D, Adler NE. Integrating Social And Medical Data To Improve Population Health: Opportunities And Barriers. Health Aff (Millwood). 2016;35(11):2116-2123.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Reconciliation by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Patients with polypharmacy in care transition settings, particularly elderly and chronically ill populations
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic medication reconciliation protocol during care transitions. Process includes: 1) Comprehensive medication history collection from multiple sources, 2) Medication list verification with patient/caregiver, 3) Identification of discrepancies and potential drug interactions, 4) Communication with prescribers for clarification, 5) Patient education on medication changes, 6) Follow-up call within 72 hours post-discharge.
expected_outcomes: Reduced medication errors by 60-75%, decreased adverse drug events, improved medication adherence rates, reduced 30-day readmission rates, enhanced patient understanding of medication regimens, improved communication between healthcare providers.
evidence_base: Chisholm-Burns MA, Kim Lee J, Spivey CA, Slack M, Herrier RN, Hall-Lipsy E, Graff Zivin J, Abraham I, Palmer J, Martin JR, Kramer SS, Wunz T. US pharmacists' effect as team members on patient care: systematic review and meta-analyses. Med Care. 2010;48(10):923-933.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Asthma Action Plan Education by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Children and adults with asthma in underserved communities, particularly those with frequent exacerbations
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive asthma education program with personalized action plans. Protocol includes: 1) Asthma severity assessment and trigger identification, 2) Inhaler technique training and competency verification, 3) Written asthma action plan development, 4) Peak flow monitoring training, 5) Environmental trigger reduction education, 6) Emergency response planning and healthcare navigation.
expected_outcomes: Improved asthma control scores, reduced asthma exacerbations (50-70% reduction), decreased emergency department visits and hospitalizations, improved inhaler technique proficiency (>90%), enhanced asthma self-management skills, improved quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Chisholm-Burns MA, Kim Lee J, Spivey CA, Slack M, Herrier RN, Hall-Lipsy E, Graff Zivin J, Abraham I, Palmer J, Martin JR, Kramer SS, Wunz T. US pharmacists' effect as team members on patient care: systematic review and meta-analyses. Med Care. 2010;48(10):923-933.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Prenatal Care Coordination by Doulas
target_population: Pregnant women in Medicaid populations, particularly those with high-risk pregnancies and social vulnerabilities
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive prenatal support and care coordination program. Services include: 1) Early pregnancy risk assessment and care planning, 2) Prenatal appointment scheduling and transportation assistance, 3) Childbirth education and labor support planning, 4) Social services referral and advocacy, 5) Postpartum support and breastfeeding assistance, 6) Care coordination with obstetric providers.
expected_outcomes: Improved prenatal care utilization (>90% adequate care), reduced preterm birth rates, increased breastfeeding initiation and duration, improved maternal satisfaction with care, reduced postpartum depression rates, decreased maternal and infant healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Peikes D, Chen A, Schore J, Brown R. Effects of care coordination on hospitalization, quality of care, and health care expenditures among Medicare beneficiaries: 15 randomized trials. JAMA. 2009;301(6):603-618.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Substance Use Screening and Brief Intervention by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults with substance use disorders in healthcare and community settings, particularly those in early recovery
implementation_guidance: Implement peer-led screening, brief intervention, and referral to treatment (SBIRT) protocol. Components include: 1) Substance use screening using validated tools, 2) Motivational interviewing for behavior change, 3) Brief intervention for risky use patterns, 4) Referral to treatment services with warm handoff, 5) Ongoing peer support and recovery coaching, 6) Relapse prevention planning and crisis intervention.
expected_outcomes: Increased engagement in substance use treatment (>70% treatment entry), reduced substance use frequency and quantity, improved treatment retention rates, enhanced recovery self-efficacy, reduced criminal justice involvement, improved employment and housing stability.
evidence_base: Eddie D, Hoffman L, Vilsaint C, Abry A, Bergman B, Hoeppner B, Weinstein C, Kelly JF. Lived experience in new models of care for substance use disorder: A systematic review of peer recovery support services and recovery coaching. Front Psychol. 2019;10:1052.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Care Transitions by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: High-risk patients transitioning from hospital to home, particularly elderly with multiple chronic conditions
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive care transitions intervention using Coleman Care Transitions Model. Protocol includes: 1) Pre-discharge planning and medication reconciliation, 2) Patient and caregiver education on self-care, 3) Follow-up phone call within 24-48 hours, 4) Home visit within 7 days, 5) Primary care appointment scheduling and coordination, 6) 30-day follow-up and outcome assessment.
expected_outcomes: Reduced 30-day readmission rates (25-40% reduction), improved patient satisfaction with care transitions, enhanced medication adherence, reduced emergency department visits, improved patient activation and self-care abilities, decreased healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Coleman EA, Parry C, Chalmers S, Min SJ. The care transitions intervention: results of a randomized controlled trial. Arch Intern Med. 2006;166(17):1822-1828.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Chronic Disease Self-Management by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with multiple chronic conditions in underserved communities, particularly racial/ethnic minorities
implementation_guidance: Implement evidence-based chronic disease self-management program adapted for community delivery. Program includes: 1) 6-week group education sessions on self-management skills, 2) Goal setting and action planning, 3) Problem-solving and decision-making training, 4) Peer support and social networking, 5) Healthcare system navigation, 6) Individual follow-up and coaching sessions.
expected_outcomes: Improved self-efficacy for managing chronic conditions, reduced hospitalizations and emergency department visits, enhanced medication adherence, improved clinical outcomes (blood pressure, blood glucose control), increased physical activity levels, improved quality of life and mental health outcomes.
evidence_base: Kim K, Choi JS, Choi E, Nieman CL, Joo JH, Lin FR, Gitlin LN, Han HR. Effects of Community-Based Health Worker Interventions to Improve Chronic Disease Management and Care Among Vulnerable Populations: A Systematic Review. Am J Public Health. 2016;106(4):e3-e28.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Heart Failure Self-Care Education by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Adults with heart failure in Medicaid populations, particularly those with frequent hospitalizations
implementation_guidance: Implement structured heart failure self-care education program. Components include: 1) Heart failure pathophysiology education, 2) Daily weight monitoring training, 3) Symptom recognition and response planning, 4) Medication adherence strategies, 5) Dietary sodium restriction counseling, 6) Activity and exercise planning, 7) When to call provider guidelines.
expected_outcomes: Reduced heart failure-related hospitalizations (30-50% reduction), improved self-care behaviors, enhanced quality of life scores, decreased emergency department visits, improved medication adherence rates, reduced healthcare costs, improved patient knowledge of heart failure management.
evidence_base: McAlister FA, Stewart S, Ferrua S, McMurray JJ. Multidisciplinary strategies for the management of heart failure patients at high risk for admission: a systematic review of randomized trials. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2004;44(4):810-819.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Chronic Kidney Disease Management by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with stages 3-5 chronic kidney disease in primary care settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive CKD management protocol. Services include: 1) CKD staging and progression monitoring, 2) Medication dosing adjustments for kidney function, 3) Blood pressure optimization, 4) Diabetes management coordination, 5) Bone and mineral disorder prevention, 6) Preparation for renal replacement therapy, 7) Patient education on kidney-healthy lifestyle.
expected_outcomes: Slowed CKD progression rates, improved blood pressure control, reduced cardiovascular events, enhanced medication safety, improved patient knowledge of CKD, delayed need for dialysis, reduced hospitalizations, improved quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Chisholm-Burns MA, Kim Lee J, Spivey CA, Slack M, Herrier RN, Hall-Lipsy E, Graff Zivin J, Abraham I, Palmer J, Martin JR, Kramer SS, Wunz T. US pharmacists' effect as team members on patient care: systematic review and meta-analyses. Med Care. 2010;48(10):923-933.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Asthma Management by Community Health Workers
target_population: Children ages 2-17 with asthma in low-income families, particularly in urban environments
implementation_guidance: Implement family-centered pediatric asthma management program. Components include: 1) Home environmental assessment and trigger reduction, 2) Caregiver education on asthma management, 3) Inhaler technique training for child and caregiver, 4) School coordination and action plan development, 5) Emergency response planning, 6) Healthcare navigation and appointment coordination.
expected_outcomes: Reduced asthma-related emergency department visits (40-60% reduction), decreased school absences, improved asthma control scores, enhanced caregiver confidence in asthma management, reduced environmental triggers in home, improved medication adherence, decreased healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Kim K, Choi JS, Choi E, Nieman CL, Joo JH, Lin FR, Gitlin LN, Han HR. Effects of Community-Based Health Worker Interventions to Improve Chronic Disease Management and Care Among Vulnerable Populations: A Systematic Review. Am J Public Health. 2016;106(4):e3-e28.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for COPD Self-Management by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with moderate to severe COPD in primary care and community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive COPD self-management education program. Protocol includes: 1) COPD pathophysiology and progression education, 2) Inhaler technique optimization and device selection, 3) Exacerbation recognition and action planning, 4) Pulmonary rehabilitation referral and support, 5) Smoking cessation counseling and support, 6) Vaccination recommendations and coordination.
expected_outcomes: Reduced COPD exacerbations (25-40% reduction), improved inhaler technique proficiency, enhanced quality of life scores, reduced hospitalizations, improved medication adherence, increased smoking cessation rates, improved exercise tolerance and functional capacity.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Obesity Prevention by Community Health Workers
target_population: Children ages 5-12 and their families in low-income communities with high obesity rates
implementation_guidance: Implement family-based childhood obesity prevention program. Components include: 1) Family nutrition education and meal planning, 2) Physical activity promotion and community resource mapping, 3) Screen time reduction strategies, 4) Healthy cooking classes and food preparation skills, 5) School and community partnership development, 6) Behavioral goal setting and tracking.
expected_outcomes: Reduced childhood obesity rates, improved dietary quality scores, increased physical activity levels, decreased screen time, enhanced family knowledge of healthy behaviors, improved BMI percentiles, increased consumption of fruits and vegetables, reduced sugar-sweetened beverage intake.
evidence_base: Kim K, Choi JS, Choi E, Nieman CL, Joo JH, Lin FR, Gitlin LN, Han HR. Effects of Community-Based Health Worker Interventions to Improve Chronic Disease Management and Care Among Vulnerable Populations: A Systematic Review. Am J Public Health. 2016;106(4):e3-e28.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Transitions of Care for Elderly Patients by Social Workers
target_population: Adults 65+ transitioning from hospital to home or skilled nursing facilities
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive discharge planning and transitions support. Services include: 1) Comprehensive discharge planning assessment, 2) Home safety evaluation and modification recommendations, 3) Community resource identification and referral, 4) Caregiver support and education, 5) Follow-up care coordination, 6) Insurance and benefits navigation, 7) Transportation arrangement support.
expected_outcomes: Reduced 30-day readmission rates, improved patient satisfaction with discharge process, enhanced caregiver preparedness, reduced emergency department visits, improved medication adherence, increased utilization of community resources, improved functional outcomes at 30 days.
evidence_base: Peikes D, Chen A, Schore J, Brown R. Effects of care coordination on hospitalization, quality of care, and health care expenditures among Medicare beneficiaries: 15 randomized trials. JAMA. 2009;301(6):603-618.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Diabetes Prevention by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults with prediabetes in primary care settings, particularly those with mental health comorbidities
implementation_guidance: Implement lifestyle intervention program for diabetes prevention. Components include: 1) Behavioral counseling for weight loss and physical activity, 2) Nutritional counseling and meal planning, 3) Stress management and coping skills training, 4) Goal setting and self-monitoring techniques, 5) Group support sessions, 6) Integration with mental health treatment plans.
expected_outcomes: Reduced progression to type 2 diabetes (40-60% reduction), significant weight loss (5-10% body weight), improved physical activity levels, enhanced dietary quality, improved mental health outcomes, increased self-efficacy for lifestyle changes, reduced cardiovascular risk factors.
evidence_base: Norris SL, Lau J, Smith SJ, Schmid CH, Engelgau MM. Self-management education for adults with type 2 diabetes: a meta-analysis of the effect on glycemic control. Diabetes Care. 2002;25(7):1159-1171.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Maternal Depression Screening by Doulas
target_population: Pregnant and postpartum women in Medicaid populations, particularly those with social risk factors
implementation_guidance: Implement perinatal depression screening and support protocol. Services include: 1) Depression screening using validated tools (PHQ-9, EPDS), 2) Risk factor assessment and safety planning, 3) Emotional support and counseling, 4) Referral to mental health services, 5) Partner and family education, 6) Postpartum follow-up and monitoring.
expected_outcomes: Increased detection of perinatal depression, improved mental health treatment engagement, reduced severity of depressive symptoms, enhanced maternal-infant bonding, improved breastfeeding outcomes, reduced postpartum complications, improved family functioning and support.
evidence_base: Bohren MA, Hofmeyr GJ, Sakala C, Fukuzawa RK, Cuthbert A. Continuous support for women during childbirth. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2017;7:CD003766.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Therapy Management by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with multiple chronic conditions and complex medication regimens
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive medication therapy management program. Services include: 1) Comprehensive medication review and assessment, 2) Identification and resolution of drug therapy problems, 3) Medication optimization and deprescribing when appropriate, 4) Patient education and counseling, 5) Coordination with prescribers, 6) Ongoing monitoring and follow-up.
expected_outcomes: Reduced medication-related problems, improved medication adherence rates, decreased adverse drug events, reduced healthcare utilization, improved clinical outcomes for chronic conditions, enhanced patient satisfaction with medication management, reduced medication costs.
evidence_base: Chisholm-Burns MA, Kim Lee J, Spivey CA, Slack M, Herrier RN, Hall-Lipsy E, Graff Zivin J, Abraham I, Palmer J, Martin JR, Kramer SS, Wunz T. US pharmacists' effect as team members on patient care: systematic review and meta-analyses. Med Care. 2010;48(10):923-933.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Immunization Outreach by Community Health Workers
target_population: Children 0-18 years in underserved communities with low vaccination rates
implementation_guidance: Implement community-based immunization outreach program. Components include: 1) Immunization status assessment and tracking, 2) Vaccine education and myth dispelling, 3) Appointment scheduling and reminder systems, 4) Transportation assistance and mobile clinic coordination, 5) School and daycare immunization requirement support, 6) Cultural competency and language-appropriate education.
expected_outcomes: Increased childhood immunization rates (>90% up-to-date status), reduced vaccine-preventable disease outbreaks, improved on-time vaccination schedules, enhanced parental knowledge and acceptance of vaccines, reduced missed opportunities for vaccination, improved school enrollment rates.
evidence_base: Kim K, Choi JS, Choi E, Nieman CL, Joo JH, Lin FR, Gitlin LN, Han HR. Effects of Community-Based Health Worker Interventions to Improve Chronic Disease Management and Care Among Vulnerable Populations: A Systematic Review. Am J Public Health. 2016;106(4):e3-e28.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Heart Failure Medication Optimization by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction in outpatient settings
implementation_guidance: Implement guideline-directed medical therapy optimization protocol. Services include: 1) Comprehensive medication review and optimization, 2) ACE inhibitor/ARB and beta-blocker titration, 3) Diuretic management and monitoring, 4) Medication adherence counseling, 5) Side effect management and monitoring, 6) Coordination with cardiology and primary care.
expected_outcomes: Improved medication adherence to guideline-directed therapy, optimized medication dosing, reduced heart failure hospitalizations, improved quality of life scores, enhanced medication knowledge, reduced medication-related adverse events, improved clinical outcomes and survival.
evidence_base: Chisholm-Burns MA, Kim Lee J, Spivey CA, Slack M, Herrier RN, Hall-Lipsy E, Graff Zivin J, Abraham I, Palmer J, Martin JR, Kramer SS, Wunz T. US pharmacists' effect as team members on patient care: systematic review and meta-analyses. Med Care. 2010;48(10):923-933.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for CKD Patient Education by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Adults with stages 3-4 chronic kidney disease in nephrology and primary care settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive CKD patient education program. Components include: 1) CKD pathophysiology and progression education, 2) Dietary counseling for kidney health, 3) Blood pressure and diabetes management education, 4) Preparation for renal replacement therapy, 5) Advance care planning discussions, 6) Coordination with nephrology and primary care.
expected_outcomes: Improved patient knowledge of CKD, enhanced self-care behaviors, better blood pressure control, improved dietary adherence, increased preparation for dialysis or transplant, improved quality of life, delayed progression to end-stage renal disease, reduced hospitalizations.
evidence_base: Martínez-González NA, Djalali S, Tandjung R, Huber-Geismann F, Markun S, Wensing M, Rosemann T. Substitution of physicians by nurses in primary care: a systematic review and meta-analysis. BMC Health Serv Res. 2014;14:214.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Adolescent Mental Health Screening by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adolescents ages 12-18 in primary care and school-based health centers
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic adolescent mental health screening program. Components include: 1) Universal screening using validated tools (PHQ-A, GAD-7), 2) Risk assessment and safety planning, 3) Brief intervention and counseling, 4) Referral to mental health services, 5) Family involvement and education, 6) School coordination and support.
expected_outcomes: Increased detection of adolescent mental health conditions, improved access to mental health treatment, reduced severity of symptoms, enhanced family understanding and support, improved school performance and attendance, reduced risk behaviors and self-harm.
evidence_base: Peikes D, Chen A, Schore J, Brown R. Effects of care coordination on hospitalization, quality of care, and health care expenditures among Medicare beneficiaries: 15 randomized trials. JAMA. 2009;301(6):603-618.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Opioid Use Disorder Treatment by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults with opioid use disorder in medication-assisted treatment programs
implementation_guidance: Implement peer recovery support services for opioid use disorder. Services include: 1) Peer counseling and support groups, 2) Medication adherence support for MAT, 3) Recovery planning and goal setting, 4) Relapse prevention strategies, 5) Social support network development, 6) Advocacy and system navigation.
expected_outcomes: Improved treatment retention rates, reduced opioid use and relapse rates, enhanced recovery self-efficacy, improved social functioning, reduced criminal justice involvement, increased employment and housing stability, improved quality of life measures.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Postpartum Care Coordination by Doulas
target_population: Postpartum women in Medicaid populations, particularly those with complications or social risk factors
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive postpartum care coordination program. Services include: 1) Postpartum health assessment and monitoring, 2) Breastfeeding support and lactation counseling, 3) Mental health screening and support, 4) Newborn care education, 5) Family planning counseling, 6) Social services referral and coordination.
expected_outcomes: Improved postpartum care utilization, increased breastfeeding duration, reduced postpartum depression rates, enhanced maternal confidence and self-efficacy, improved newborn health outcomes, reduced postpartum complications, increased family planning uptake.
evidence_base: Peikes D, Chen A, Schore J, Brown R. Effects of care coordination on hospitalization, quality of care, and health care expenditures among Medicare beneficiaries: 15 randomized trials. JAMA. 2009;301(6):603-618.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Transitions from Pediatric to Adult Care by Social Workers
target_population: Adolescents and young adults ages 16-25 with chronic conditions transitioning to adult care
implementation_guidance: Implement structured healthcare transition program. Components include: 1) Transition readiness assessment, 2) Self-advocacy and healthcare navigation training, 3) Adult provider identification and coordination, 4) Insurance and benefits transition support, 5) Care plan transfer and coordination, 6) Ongoing support during transition period.
expected_outcomes: Improved transition readiness scores, successful transfer to adult care providers, maintained continuity of care, enhanced self-management skills, reduced gaps in care, improved health outcomes during transition, increased patient satisfaction with transition process.
evidence_base: Peikes D, Chen A, Schore J, Brown R. Effects of care coordination on hospitalization, quality of care, and health care expenditures among Medicare beneficiaries: 15 randomized trials. JAMA. 2009;301(6):603-618.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Cardiovascular Risk Reduction by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with cardiovascular risk factors in underserved communities
implementation_guidance: Implement community-based cardiovascular risk reduction program. Components include: 1) Cardiovascular risk assessment and education, 2) Blood pressure monitoring and management support, 3) Lifestyle counseling for diet and physical activity, 4) Smoking cessation support, 5) Medication adherence assistance, 6) Healthcare navigation and appointment coordination.
expected_outcomes: Reduced cardiovascular risk scores, improved blood pressure control, increased physical activity levels, enhanced dietary quality, increased smoking cessation rates, improved medication adherence, reduced cardiovascular events, decreased healthcare costs.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Asthma Management in Schools by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: School-age children with asthma in elementary and middle schools
implementation_guidance: Implement school-based asthma management program. Components include: 1) School asthma policy development and implementation, 2) Staff training on asthma management and emergency response, 3) Student asthma education and self-management training, 4) Environmental trigger assessment and reduction, 5) Medication administration protocols, 6) Parent and healthcare provider communication.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Developmental Screening by Community Health Workers
target_population: Children ages 0-5 years in underserved communities at risk for developmental delays
implementation_guidance: Implement community-based developmental screening program. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Mental Health Crisis Intervention by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults with serious mental illness in community mental health settings
implementation_guidance: Implement peer-led crisis intervention and support program. Services include: 1) Crisis assessment and de-escalation, 2) Safety planning and risk assessment, 3) Peer counseling and support, 4) Resource identification and referral, 5) Follow-up and ongoing support, 6) Advocacy and system navigation.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Prenatal Substance Use Screening by Social Workers
target_population: Pregnant women in prenatal care settings, particularly those with risk factors for substance use
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive prenatal substance use screening and intervention program. Components include: 1) Universal substance use screening using validated tools, 2) Brief intervention and motivational interviewing, 3) Referral to treatment services, 4) Case management and support services, 5) Coordination with obstetric care, 6) Child welfare and safety planning.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Transitions from Hospital to Home by Care Coordinators
target_population: Adults with complex medical conditions transitioning from hospital to home
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive hospital-to-home transition program. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Depression Screening and Brief Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Adults in primary care and community settings with suspected or confirmed depression
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic depression screening using PHQ-9 with stepped care approach. Protocol includes: 1) Universal screening at intake and follow-up visits, 2) Risk assessment for suicidality using Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale, 3) Brief behavioral activation for mild depression, 4) Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) for moderate depression, 5) Warm handoff to psychiatry for severe depression, 6) Care coordination with primary care provider, 7) Follow-up assessment at 2, 4, and 8 weeks.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Motivational Interviewing for Chronic Disease Self-Management by Social Workers

expected_outcomes: Cognitive-behavioral therapy for chronic pain (CBT-CP); acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) for pain; mindfulness-based stress reduction; pain self-management education; opioid tapering support; non-pharmacologic pain management strategies; care coordination with pain management and primary care; psychiatric medication management for comorbid conditions
evidence_base: Woltmann E, Grogan-Kaylor A, Perron B, Georges H, Kilbourne AM, Bauer MS. Comparative effectiveness of collaborative chronic care models for mental health conditions across primary, specialty, and behavioral health care settings: systematic review and meta-analysis. Am J Psychiatry. 2012;169(8):790-804.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Suicide Prevention Care Management by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults at elevated suicide risk in primary care, emergency departments, and community settings
implementation_guidance: Suicide risk assessment using C-SSRS or similar validated tool; mental health disorder assessment; substance use assessment; access to lethal means assessment; protective factors assessment; prior suicide attempts; social support assessment; barriers to treatment
expected_outcomes: Safety planning intervention; lethal means counseling and restriction; crisis resource connection (988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline); brief interventions (CAMS, DBT skills); intensive follow-up contact (caring contacts, phone calls); psychiatric consultation and medication management; care coordination; family psychoeducation; peer support connection
evidence_base: Peikes D, Chen A, Schore J, Brown R. Effects of care coordination on hospitalization, quality of care, and health care expenditures among Medicare beneficiaries: 15 randomized trials. JAMA. 2009;301(6):603-618.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Continuous Labor Support by Doulas
target_population: Pregnant women in labor in hospital and birth center settings
implementation_guidance: Labor progress assessment (non-clinical observation); pain and coping assessment; emotional state assessment; support needs assessment; birth preferences review; partner/family support assessment
expected_outcomes: Continuous labor support and presence; comfort measures (positioning, massage, breathing techniques, hydrotherapy); emotional support and encouragement; information provision; advocacy and communication facilitation with medical team; partner/family support and coaching; birth preference support
evidence_base: Bohren MA, Hofmeyr GJ, Sakala C, Fukuzawa RK, Cuthbert A. Continuous support for women during childbirth. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2017;7:CD003766.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Prenatal Education and Birth Planning by Doulas
target_population: Pregnant women, particularly first-time mothers and those in underserved communities
implementation_guidance: Pregnancy knowledge and education needs assessment; birth preferences and values assessment; fears and concerns assessment; social support assessment; cultural beliefs and practices assessment; access to prenatal care assessment
expected_outcomes: Prenatal education (labor stages, pain management options, medical interventions, postpartum care); birth plan development; childbirth preparation classes; prenatal visits and relationship building; resource connection (prenatal care, WIC, childbirth classes); partner/family education; cultural advocacy
evidence_base: Bohren MA, Hofmeyr GJ, Sakala C, Fukuzawa RK, Cuthbert A. Continuous support for women during childbirth. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2017;7:CD003766.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Postpartum Support by Doulas
target_population: Postpartum women and newborns, particularly those at risk for postpartum complications or with limited social support
implementation_guidance: Postpartum recovery assessment; breastfeeding assessment; newborn care knowledge assessment; maternal mental health screening (EPDS); social support assessment; household needs assessment; warning signs knowledge assessment
expected_outcomes: Postpartum home visits; breastfeeding support and education; newborn care education (bathing, diapering, sleep safety, feeding cues); maternal self-care education; emotional support; household assistance; postpartum warning signs education; resource connection; partner/family support; postpartum depression screening and referral
evidence_base: Bohren MA, Hofmeyr GJ, Sakala C, Fukuzawa RK, Cuthbert A. Continuous support for women during childbirth. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2017;7:CD003766.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Breastfeeding Support by Doulas
target_population: Pregnant and postpartum women planning to breastfeed or experiencing breastfeeding challenges
implementation_guidance: Breastfeeding intentions and goals assessment; breastfeeding knowledge assessment; latch and positioning assessment; milk supply concerns assessment; barriers to breastfeeding assessment; support system assessment; cultural beliefs about breastfeeding
expected_outcomes: Prenatal breastfeeding education; immediate postpartum breastfeeding support; latch and positioning assistance; breastfeeding problem-solving (sore nipples, engorgement, low milk supply concerns); pumping and milk storage education; returning to work/school support; lactation consultant referral when needed; emotional support and encouragement
evidence_base: Bohren MA, Hofmeyr GJ, Sakala C, Fukuzawa RK, Cuthbert A. Continuous support for women during childbirth. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2017;7:CD003766.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Supporting Adolescent Mothers by Doulas
target_population: Pregnant and parenting adolescents (ages 13-19)
implementation_guidance: Developmental and maturity assessment; pregnancy and parenting knowledge assessment; social support assessment; educational and vocational goals assessment; mental health screening; intimate partner violence screening; housing and financial stability assessment
expected_outcomes: Developmentally appropriate prenatal and postpartum education; continuous labor support; parenting skills education; goal-setting and life planning support; social support building; resource connection (WIC, housing, education, childcare); mental health support and referral; family engagement when appropriate; advocacy
evidence_base: Bohren MA, Hofmeyr GJ, Sakala C, Fukuzawa RK, Cuthbert A. Continuous support for women during childbirth. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2017;7:CD003766.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Supporting High-Risk Pregnancies by Doulas
target_population: Women with high-risk pregnancies (gestational diabetes, hypertension, preterm labor risk, multiple gestation, advanced maternal age)
implementation_guidance: Understanding of high-risk condition and medical plan; emotional response to high-risk diagnosis; support needs assessment; barriers to prenatal care and treatment adherence; stress and anxiety assessment; social support assessment
expected_outcomes: Emotional support and reassurance; education about high-risk condition (non-clinical); prenatal care attendance support; treatment adherence support; stress reduction techniques; birth planning adapted to high-risk status; communication facilitation with medical team; partner/family support; resource connection; postpartum support adapted to needs
evidence_base: Bohren MA, Hofmeyr GJ, Sakala C, Fukuzawa RK, Cuthbert A. Continuous support for women during childbirth. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2017;7:CD003766.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Culturally Responsive Doula Care
target_population: Pregnant and postpartum women from diverse cultural backgrounds, particularly immigrant and refugee communities
implementation_guidance: Cultural beliefs and practices about pregnancy, birth, and postpartum; language preferences and needs; traditional practices and preferences; family structure and decision-making; cultural dietary practices; immigration status and related concerns; experiences of discrimination
expected_outcomes: Culturally tailored prenatal and postpartum education; language-concordant support or interpretation coordination; incorporation of cultural practices when safe and desired; cultural advocacy with medical team; addressing cultural conflicts or misunderstandings; community resource connection; addressing immigration-related barriers; culturally appropriate nutrition counseling
evidence_base: Bohren MA, Hofmeyr GJ, Sakala C, Fukuzawa RK, Cuthbert A. Continuous support for women during childbirth. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2017;7:CD003766.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Supporting Cesarean Birth and Recovery by Doulas
target_population: Women having planned or unplanned cesarean births
implementation_guidance: Understanding of cesarean indication and procedure; emotional response to cesarean (especially if unplanned); support needs assessment; birth preferences within cesarean context; postoperative recovery knowledge; breastfeeding intentions; social support for recovery
expected_outcomes: Emotional support before, during, and after cesarean; education about cesarean procedure and recovery; birth preference advocacy within cesarean context (e.g., gentle cesarean options); support during cesarean when permitted; immediate postpartum support; cesarean recovery education; breastfeeding support after cesarean; pain management education; scar care education; emotional processing of birth experience
evidence_base: Bohren MA, Hofmeyr GJ, Sakala C, Fukuzawa RK, Cuthbert A. Continuous support for women during childbirth. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2017;7:CD003766.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Peer Support for Opioid Use Disorder Recovery by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults with opioid use disorder in medication-assisted treatment (MAT) programs and recovery
implementation_guidance: Recovery stage and goals assessment; treatment engagement and adherence assessment; barriers to recovery assessment; social support assessment; housing and employment status; relapse risk assessment; peer support needs and preferences
expected_outcomes: Peer mentorship and support; sharing lived experience of opioid recovery; MAT adherence support; recovery goal-setting and planning; coping skills and relapse prevention support; recovery community connection; mutual aid group facilitation; addressing stigma; crisis support; celebrating recovery milestones

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Peer Support for Mental Health Recovery by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults with serious mental illness (schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depression) in community mental health settings
implementation_guidance: Recovery stage and goals assessment; psychiatric symptom and functioning assessment; medication adherence assessment; social support and isolation assessment; employment and housing status; wellness and self-care practices; hope and empowerment assessment
expected_outcomes: Peer support and mentorship; sharing lived experience of mental health recovery; wellness and recovery action planning (WRAP); medication adherence support; social connection and community integration; employment and education support; crisis planning and support; self-advocacy skills building; hope and empowerment promotion
evidence_base: Eddie D, Hoffman L, Vilsaint C, Abry A, Bergman B, Hoeppner B, Weinstein C, Kelly JF. Lived experience in new models of care for substance use disorder: A systematic review of peer recovery support services and recovery coaching. Front Psychol. 2019;10:1052.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Peer Recovery Support in Emergency Departments by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults presenting to emergency departments with substance use-related concerns or overdoses
implementation_guidance: Immediate needs and safety assessment; readiness for treatment assessment; prior treatment history; barriers to treatment engagement; social support assessment; housing and basic needs assessment; overdose risk assessment
expected_outcomes: Peer engagement and rapport building in ED; motivational support for treatment; warm handoff to treatment services; naloxone distribution and education; recovery resource information; follow-up contact and support; addressing stigma and shame; hope and possibility messaging; crisis support
evidence_base: Eddie D, Hoffman L, Vilsaint C, Abry A, Bergman B, Hoeppner B, Weinstein C, Kelly JF. Lived experience in new models of care for substance use disorder: A systematic review of peer recovery support services and recovery coaching. Front Psychol. 2019;10:1052.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Peer Recovery Support for Co-Occurring Disorders by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults with co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders
implementation_guidance: Mental health and substance use assessment; integrated treatment engagement; medication adherence for both conditions; social support and housing; employment status; recovery goals for both conditions; barriers to integrated treatment
expected_outcomes: Peer support for integrated recovery; sharing lived experience of co-occurring disorder recovery; integrated treatment engagement support; medication adherence support; dual recovery mutual aid connection; wellness and recovery planning; crisis support; addressing stigma; social connection and community integration
evidence_base: Eddie D, Hoffman L, Vilsaint C, Abry A, Bergman B, Hoeppner B, Weinstein C, Kelly JF. Lived experience in new models of care for substance use disorder: A systematic review of peer recovery support services and recovery coaching. Front Psychol. 2019;10:1052.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Peer Recovery Support for Criminal Justice-Involved Individuals by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults with substance use disorders involved in criminal justice system (jail, prison, probation, drug court)
implementation_guidance: Criminal justice status and requirements; substance use and treatment history; reentry needs and barriers; housing and employment barriers; family and social support; trauma history; motivation for recovery; legal obligations
expected_outcomes: Peer support during incarceration and reentry; treatment linkage and engagement; recovery planning; addressing reentry barriers (housing, employment, ID, benefits); family reunification support; criminal justice system navigation; drug court support; trauma-informed peer support; building pro-social supports
evidence_base: Eddie D, Hoffman L, Vilsaint C, Abry A, Bergman B, Hoeppner B, Weinstein C, Kelly JF. Lived experience in new models of care for substance use disorder: A systematic review of peer recovery support services and recovery coaching. Front Psychol. 2019;10:1052.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Peer Recovery Support for Pregnant and Parenting Women by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Pregnant and parenting women with substance use disorders
implementation_guidance: Substance use and recovery status; prenatal care engagement; parenting needs and child welfare involvement; housing and safety; mental health and trauma; social support; barriers to treatment and recovery; infant health and development
expected_outcomes: Peer support for recovery during pregnancy and parenting; prenatal care engagement support; treatment retention support; parenting skills support; child welfare system navigation; trauma-informed peer support; mother-infant bonding support; addressing shame and stigma; recovery community connection; family preservation support
evidence_base: Eddie D, Hoffman L, Vilsaint C, Abry A, Bergman B, Hoeppner B, Weinstein C, Kelly JF. Lived experience in new models of care for substance use disorder: A systematic review of peer recovery support services and recovery coaching. Front Psychol. 2019;10:1052.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Peer Recovery Support for Youth and Young Adults by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Youth and young adults (ages 16-25) with substance use disorders
implementation_guidance: Substance use patterns and severity; educational and vocational status; family relationships and support; peer influences; mental health and trauma; housing stability; legal involvement; developmental needs; recovery readiness
expected_outcomes: Developmentally appropriate peer support; sharing lived experience of young adult recovery; treatment engagement support; educational and vocational goal support; healthy peer relationship building; family relationship support; recovery-oriented activities; addressing stigma; crisis support; transition to adult services support
evidence_base: Eddie D, Hoffman L, Vilsaint C, Abry A, Bergman B, Hoeppner B, Weinstein C, Kelly JF. Lived experience in new models of care for substance use disorder: A systematic review of peer recovery support services and recovery coaching. Front Psychol. 2019;10:1052.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Peer-Led Mutual Aid and Recovery Support Groups by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults in recovery from substance use disorders seeking peer support and community
implementation_guidance: Recovery stage and needs; mutual aid experience and preferences; social support and isolation; recovery goals; barriers to mutual aid participation; cultural and linguistic needs; transportation and accessibility needs
expected_outcomes: Facilitation of peer-led recovery support groups; mutual aid meeting facilitation (SMART Recovery, Refuge Recovery, etc.); recovery topic education; sharing recovery stories; group cohesion building; recovery community building; addressing barriers to participation; cultural adaptation of groups; virtual and in-person options; recovery celebration
evidence_base: Eddie D, Hoffman L, Vilsaint C, Abry A, Bergman B, Hoeppner B, Weinstein C, Kelly JF. Lived experience in new models of care for substance use disorder: A systematic review of peer recovery support services and recovery coaching. Front Psychol. 2019;10:1052.
